newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's forces kill 10 rebels in Algiers - paper.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's forces kill 10 rebels in Algiers - paper.

text.p: Algerian security forces killed 10 Moslem guerrillas suspected of murdering civilians and members of government forces in Algiers, Algeria's El Watan newspaper said on Tuesday.
The paper, well informed on security matters, said eight rebels were shot dead on Saturday in Climat de France suburb, a hotbed for Moslem guerrilla on the northern edge of Algiers.
The group had been active in four sectors in the Algerian capital, and had killed civilians opposed to Moslem guerrillas, it added.
Two others, trying to steal a car, were killed on Sunday in Leveilly neighbourhood by a police patrol.

The authorities blame Moslem guerrillas for a series of car bombings in the past four years. About 1,400 civilians have been killed in bomb attacks in the past 24 months, according to an official report released last month.
The killing of the 10 guerrillas coincided with a two-day national conference in Algiers grouping 1,000 politicians and Algeria's leadership to chart reforms on the country's future.

Thirty-eight party, union and other leaders signed a pact on Sunday at the end of the National conference, which was boycotted by main secular opposition parties and from which radical Islamists have been barred.
The pact, which bans use of Islam, Arabic and Berber languages as political weapons to win power, condemns violence and lays the foundations for a multi-party democracy.
President Liamine Zeroual said the conference gave a clear message for "those led blindly by aberration and despair into a vain and suicidal adventure against their homeland."
An estimated 50,000 people have died in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
